root.name: Slav Defense: Czech Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5

overview: Black takes on c4 and develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain, while White stops ...b5 with a4. The main line is 6.e3 e6 7.Bxc4 Bb4 8.O-O Nbd7, with Black developed and sound and White having a small space edge. Sharper options include 6.Ne5 (Krause Attack).

white_ideas.idea: e3, Bxc4 and O-O, then Qe2 or e4 to claim space and use the pawn centre.
Ne5 and Qb3 ideas against Black's queenside.

black_ideas.idea: ...e6, ...Bb4 and ...Nbd7, with ...Bg6 or ...O-O and ...c5 or ...e5 break.
Develop the c8 bishop actively and hit the centre with ...c5 or ...e5.

typical_structures.structure: Slav structure with the c-pawn exchanged for the c4 pawn, White d4/e3 against Black c6/e6 or ...e5.

character.notes: Black gets a sound, developed position, hard to break down; the Krause Attack is sharper.

gambit.notes: The c4 pawn is regained by White.

soundness.notes: Fully sound; one of the main Slav lines.

structure.notes: Asymmetric semi-open centre with d4 and ...c6/e6, or an open e-file after ...e5.

level.notes: Black needs sound plans and a few forced lines; no deep theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Krause Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharper, hitting c4 and f7 with tactics.

character.reason: Slav set-up that is sound and hard to break down.

gambit.reason: The pawn is regained by Bxc4.

structure.reason: One side has an asymmetrical centre and the c- and d-files are partly open.

approach.reason: A regular line at all levels.

level.reason: Clear development plans and moderate theory.

plans.reason: No single recognised plan from the list dominates.
